title: Accountability and Responsibility
learningGoal: Understand the difference between excuses, explanations, and accountability in behaviour change.
microLesson: Accountability means recognising choices, acknowledging harm, and taking responsibility without minimising, denying, or blaming.
activity: Rewrite three past behaviours using accountable language.

title: Understanding Harm
learningGoal: Recognise the emotional, psychological, and physical harm caused by abusive behaviour.
microLesson: Harm includes fear, trauma, loss of autonomy, damaged relationships, and long-term emotional impacts.
activity: Analyse a case study and identify all forms of harm caused.

title: Patterns of Abusive Behaviour
learningGoal: Identify personal patterns of abusive behaviour and triggers.
microLesson: Abusive behaviour often follows patterns: escalation, control tactics, emotional withdrawal, or coercion.

title: Emotional Regulation for Behaviour Change
learningGoal: Learn emotional regulation strategies to prevent harmful behaviour.
microLesson: Emotional dysregulation contributes to harmful behaviour. Techniques include grounding, time-outs, and recognising early warning signs.
activity: Practice a 5-minute regulation exercise and reflect on its impact.

title: Respectful Communication
learningGoal: Develop communication skills that support non-violence and respect.
microLesson: Respectful communication includes listening, non-threatening language, emotional honesty, and avoiding manipulation.
activity: Rewrite three past conversations using respectful communication techniques.

title: Partner-Safety Integration
learningGoal: Understand how behaviour change connects to partner and child safety.
microLesson: Behaviour change programs prioritise partner and child safety through monitoring, accountability, and safe contact protocols.
activity: Identify three ways behaviour change can improve partner safety.

title: Behaviour-Change Commitment
learningGoal: Commit to specific, measurable behaviour-change actions.
microLesson: Sustainable change requires clear commitments, accountability structures, and ongoing reflection.
activity: Write a 200-word behaviour-change commitment with three measurable actions.
